references.text: Moses conveys the Lord's words to the people, and the people answer in unison. This illustrates the pattern where Moses serves as an intermediary between God and the children of Israel.
The preceding verse where Moses first calls for Aaron and the leaders before the entire congregation approaches, serving as direct context for verse 32.
Moses goes down to the people and speaks to them at Mount Sinai, establishing the pattern of Moses' role as a mediator of God's words from the mountain.
The Lord calls Moses up on the mountain to give him the laws and commandments that Moses will later teach the people.
God commands Moses to stand with Him to receive all the commandments and statutes that he is to teach the children of Israel.
Moses is to teach the people the commandments and statutes that the Lord has commanded, parallel to the mediation at Sinai.
Moses gathers the entire congregation of Israel and tells them what the Lord has commanded, continuing the mediation from chapter 34.
Paul refers to Moses' radiant face and the legislation at Sinai as background for the glory of the new covenant.
Highlights Moses' unique role as God's spokesperson in the transmission of specific laws.
Lev 27:34 confirms and summarizes the same giving of the commandments on Sinai as described in Ex 34:32.
